correctness.rationale: The classification follows by whether the involution fixes or swaps the two primitive idempotents in the neutral diagonal component. The fixed case gives sigma_a with a in F^×; the swapped case gives exactly two signs. Graded automorphisms are induced by monomial matrices, changing a only by a square or inversion, so square classes are exact invariants. After adjoining a square root of a/b the sigma_a forms become graded-isomorphic, and scalar-extension invariance in characteristic zero gives equality of their graded *-identity ideals and central-polynomial spaces.

originality.rationale: Qualified to the best of our knowledge. The square-class/discriminant phenomenon itself is standard. The recent source arXiv:2609.20488v1 states arbitrary characteristic zero but invokes a graded-involution classification whose cited Bahturin-Zaicev source assumes an algebraically closed field. Targeted searches did not locate a public correction or an explicit square-class completion together with the graded-PI and central-PI equivalence of the missing forms.

value.rationale: The result supplies a sharp replacement for the affected classification branch, produces infinitely many omitted classes over fields such as Q, and simultaneously shows that the downstream transpose-class polynomial-identity and central-polynomial formulas extend to all of those forms without new computations.
